messages:
lee: heads up — since ~09:35 we’re seeing controller-manager restart cycles in ap-south1. GPU provisioning queue is growing, jobs stuck in Pending with Attach errors.
olga: seen similar alerts. any obvious correlation with apiserver?
sam: spikes in apiserver leader heartbeat jitter earlier? i glanced at controlplane metrics and saw a burst of leader re-elections around 09:34.
lee: yep, leader changes + controller restart churn. logs show repeated lease renew failures: 
```
I0328 09:34:12.123 controller.go:254] failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded
I0328 09:34:12.124 controller.go:260] triggering restart for safety
```
sam: i also pulled kubelet/gpu-provisioner logs — attach plugin timed out: 
```
ERROR attach: timeout waiting for device: nvme-attach error code 110
```
maria: might be two separate symptoms — controlplane leader jitter causes controllers to reconnect; that plus node-level attach latency leads to backlog. any networking hiccups in that AZ?
lee: netmetrics show increased RTOs on the NAT gateway in the same window. outbound SNAT port exhaustion spikes at 09:33.
aj: that would explain controller leases failing (can't reach apiserver) and the node attach RPCs timing out when contacting cloud API. can we throttle outbound or add ephemeral SNAT capacity?
infra-bot: alert: ap-south1-nat-gateway-snat-utilization=98% for TGW-prod-01 (09:33:40). Related incidents: none open.
olga: temporary mitigation: bump controller-manager lease renewal timeout in the deployment to 20s? risky but buys time. alternatively, point controllers to standby apiserver in same region to reduce cross-AZ hops.
lee: pushing a quick change to controller-manager args (renew-deadline=20s) in staging now to observe. if green, we can patch prod with rolling restart.
sam: also recommend enabling conservative attach retry backoff on the provisioner so it doesn't spam cloud API during SNAT saturation. config snippet: 
```yaml
provisioner:
  attach:
    backoff:
      initial: 1s
      factor: 2
      max: 30s
```
maria: agree on both. long-term fix: increase NAT capacity or move heavy attach traffic through a proxy with pooled connections and fewer ports. note cost tradeoff.
aj: on cost — adding another NAT gateway is ~+$0.35/hr and additional egress data charges. but the SLA hit from stuck workflows likely costlier.
oncall-bot: runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ctrlplane-lease-drift>. recommended steps executed: 1) set renew-deadline=20s (staging), 2) enable attach backoff (staging), 3) monitor SNAT.
lee: staging change looks stable after 2m, controller restarts stopped and attach retry queue shrank. rolling prod patch in 10m unless objections.
olga: thumbs up from me. also capture logs for postmortem and add a smoke test for SNAT port usage during large attach storms.
lee: will open a short postmortem ticket and tag networking + infra. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
